contract: Supervised host for the assembly/run-engine Runs of one node, for text model calls of integration/ai-text: start_link takes owner_id (1..200 bytes), max_runs (a reservation table from start_run/3 or wake/2 through confirmed teardown; the host's own Registry and dedicated Unit DynamicSupervisor with max_children max_runs for one DynamicUnits directory with idle_ms), Unit, Run, evidence, EffectIntent journal and activation Store views of one namespace, one Lease over the Run view (clock :store on PostgreSQL, one manual-clock backend on Memory), the engine clock, lease_ttl_ms (1..86,400,000) and the spec callback, and optionally fencing_proof, on_terminal, on_lost and allow_volatile. A spec holds the stable Run, operation, Attempt and Unit identities (Run owner stream and lease key run/<unit>, evidence stream evidence/<unit>), provider_refs, tenant, principal, pattern, schemas, its finish, ask_person and nested_callable bindings (any other kind is refused at start as outside_profile), the AI binding descriptors, gate, context, Budget, budget_rule, request cap, Run deadline and the result reader's retention. start_run/3 reserves, claims the lease key, provisions the EffectIntent startup bindings once, starts the Run owner, creates the Run and begins the spec's Attempt (a retry gets {:unchanged, :duplicate, _} and begins none), and starts the evidence Writer, AsyncWork and the engine with result_reader; a lease another owner holds is {:error, {:lease_refused, refusal}} with no engine. input/5, control/5, status/2, deadlines/2, result/4 and transcript/4 pass through ({:error, :not_running} for a Run not live on this host); control/5 forwards no Approval or begin_attempt control; after a terminal outcome input/5 and control/5 give {:error, :terminal} and on_terminal is called; reap/2 stops and confirms every per-Run process, releases the lease and frees the slot. AI bindings: the idempotency key is the SHA-256 of {run_id, attempt_id, action_id}; an ai-text admission refusal is a gate denial recorded before any intent (no intent, no provider call); facts/1 repeats the passed admission with no I/O; every sink delivery goes to the Run's worker, which routes it by the committed model_call actions of the transcript and the binding configuration (held until verified at a start or wake) into one action_outcome input under an ID of Run, Attempt and occurrence, whose frame and whole context (a future pause_deadline from the trusted context under budget_rule :pause) the first submission fixes for every retry and duplicate; completed is completed/dispatched with the descriptor's usage conversion as actual (none without reported usage), refused is not_dispatched with actual 0 only for credentials_unavailable and input_unavailable and dispatched otherwise, unknown is unknown dispatch with no actual except malformed_response (dispatched), each under elzoo.ai-text.result v1 in the README's completed or refusal view; sink_failed gives no input and is reported. wake/2 gives one disposition per Run (:woken or a README reason), opens only Runs with a current Attempt, rebuilds the spec (another fingerprint is incompatible_recovery with the Unit stopped and confirmed), and before any engine requires confirmed teardown by this host with no Run-stream write since, or a fresh :fenced from fencing_proof asked at each check, else fencing_unproven with no engine and no activation granted. One wake timer per Run from deadlines/1 (while paused the earlier of the Run and pause deadlines), refreshed after each start, wake, input and control, sends one wake under a digest ID of Run, Attempt and deadline; a replaced timer sends none. Lease renewal through RunApprovalRelease.renew/2 half the TTL before the lease-clock expiry estimate; a lease_lost, fenced, indeterminate or unknown result, a renewal that exits on its caller timeout, or no confirmed renewal by the estimate stops admission ({:error, :lease_lost}), fences the Run's processes and calls on_lost; only an indeterminate result keeps a receipt for reconcile:.
limits: One node: the host fences only processes that it tracked from their start (the worker reports its own, the activation callback each EffectIntent owner); a predecessor on another node, or of an earlier host incarnation, needs the caller's fencing_proof, which this Piece cannot check. A confirmed-teardown marker lives in the host process only. Two hosts in one VM stand for two nodes in the tests; one host per node is not enforced.

Profile: protocol version 1, no expiry_reports or messages option, no local work, Resource, outside event, tool call or other Effect binding, so no asynchronous engine input bypasses the host and the deadlines and terminal phase are read only at the refresh points. ASK model calls wait until the Run ends; a Run keeps the spec's Attempt.

Routes are read from the whole retained transcript (at most 65,536 records and 536,870,912 bytes): beyond that, and for a key that no committed action gives, an outcome is reported and not given to the engine. Sink deliveries are volatile: a delivery lost with the worker leaves its slot open, and no reconciliation of intents is supplied; the intent's durable settlement can differ from the engine's slot.

A host input that the engine answers {:error, :unavailable} or an exit is sent again under the same ID, frame and context at most 20 times (200 ms times the attempt), then reported; a refused input is reported. A trusted context that gives no future pause deadline is outside the engine's Need: the outcome is reported and not submitted, a wake is tried again a second later.

Renewal and expiry are timed on the node's monotonic clock from the moment before each lease call (until - at of a token is the TTL), sound for a lease clock that does not run faster than that clock; on Memory the manual clock must not be moved faster. A renewal that waits the whole 5,000 ms caller limit ends before the estimate only for a TTL of 10 s or more; with a smaller TTL it is the estimate (on_lost :expired) that stops admission. {:error, :lease_lost} is admission, not a physical fence: an input already with the worker can reach the engine until the teardown stops it.
The wake timer waits the difference of the engine clock's milliseconds on the node's timers: a Run deadline is reached on time only with an engine clock that runs in real time.
Reports are Logger warnings with the Run reference and the action or key, never a payload; no telemetry event. on_terminal and on_lost run in host tasks, once per incarnation of a Run.

Finite disposable-PostgreSQL scenarios with two Memory scenarios and the scripted Req stub of integration/ai-text-anthropic: no live provider, no production fencing, cluster ownership or exactly-once external effect is shown.

grounding.claim: The groups end_to_end, model_call_not_completed, capacity and options_and_profile: an AgentLoop Run started with start_run/3 and its typed start through input/5 answers with the scripted stub, result/4 returns the completed record before reap/2 and {:error, :not_running} after it, on disposable PostgreSQL and on one Memory namespace whose fold and limits admit every owner's writes, with one manual-clock Lease backend and allow_volatile; a model call answered 500 ends the Run failed with no host cancel and {:failed, record} (model_call_not_completed) before reap; with max_runs 2 held by a terminal Run and a Run whose Unit sleeps, a third start is {:error, :capacity}, and reap/2 leaves no process of that Run (each tracked process dead and the VM process count back to its value before the Run), the lease free and a start admitted; options and profile refusals.

The groups admission_refusal, sink_route and translation: an image part is a gate denial unsupported_feature settled refused with no intent stream, no activation record and no stub request; the intent key is ai-text's key of the SHA-256 of {run_id, attempt_id, action_id}, the input ID is 67 bytes from Run, Attempt and occurrence, and a duplicate sink delivery (traced) is the same input answered {:ok, :duplicate} with one settlement; under budget_rule :pause the duplicate keeps the first pause deadline after the context changed; a transport timeout commits dispatch unknown with no actual; a sink_failed delivery gives no input and the slot stays running; every ai-text outcome has its input form.

The groups crash_and_wake, routing, fingerprint_and_dispositions and lease_fencing: with the stub blocked inside the call, a killed engine is torn down and woken on the same host, and a host on another stand-in node (its own group leader) frozen past its lease is taken over by a second host whose fencing_proof stops every process of that node; in each the stub is called once, the slot settles unknown once with lost_outcome and the Run reads failed with model_call_not_completed; lease expiry alone with no proof is fencing_unproven with no activation record and no new send; a start_run/3 retry on an existing journal passes by confirmed teardown on the same host (create and begin_attempt answer duplicate, one Attempt) and is fencing_unproven on a new host incarnation; the proof is asked at each check (fenced, then unproven); an untried intent first dispatched during a wake is held in the worker until the route is verified and settles once; a changed gate version or request cap is incompatible_recovery with the Unit stopped while the batch wakes another Run; a Run with no current Attempt and one whose lease another owner holds give one disposition each and leave no process; a second host's start or wake on a held key is the lease refusal on PostgreSQL and, with one shared Lease backend, on Memory.

The groups deadlines and renewal: an idle Run ends out_of_time by the host's wake at its deadline; a paused Run ends at the earlier deadline in both orderings (a pause control whose pause deadline is after the Run deadline, and a Budget exhaustion under budget_rule :pause whose pause deadline comes first), each wake under the digest ID of that deadline; a continue that replaces the Run deadline moves the timer and the old deadline gives no wake; a Run lives through three TTLs of 1,000 ms (six inputs 500 ms apart, each applied) with the lease renewed at least four times, then completes; a seized lease is lost (on_lost lease_lost), admission stops and every process of the Run ends; a renewal whose reply is held 6 s, past the 5 s caller limit, is on_lost {:unknown, :no_receipt}, the host stays alive with admission stopped, the old owner is gone before the wake that replaces it, the late renewal committed, and no receipt is kept.
Pinned GenServer, Registry, DynamicSupervisor, Task.Supervisor and Process link, monitor and timer semantics carry the host, its workers, the teardown and the timers; no local OTP runtime proof.
OTP 29.1.3 exit signals (an untrappable kill), links, monitors, group-leader inheritance (the tests' stand-in node) and ETF/SHA-256 for the derived identities.

The caller supplies compatible Store views of one namespace, a Lease over the Run view, trusted callbacks (a spec rebuilt from durable facts with stable identities, a context that gives a future pause deadline when sampled, a prompt clock in real time) and a fencing_proof that answers :fenced only when every predecessor that could act or write is fenced, also on another node; it supervises the host, gives each Run one stable run_ref and Unit identity, and keeps full retained history. Scripted stubs and local PostgreSQL do not establish production fencing or provider behaviour.

telemetry.contract: OTP diagnostics and a Logger warning (Run reference and action or key, no payload) for a delivery that gives the engine no input: a sink failure, no route, no future pause deadline, a refused or untaken input; no custom event or exporter.

config.contract: Fixed construction options (owner_id, max_runs, idle_ms, the five Store views, Lease, clock, lease_ttl_ms, spec callback; optional fencing_proof, on_terminal, on_lost, allow_volatile, name) refused as invalid_options when missing, out of range or of mixed namespaces; per-Run specs checked at start; no hot change.

control.contract: start_run/3, wake/2 (one disposition per Run), reap/2 with confirmed teardown, and pass-through input/5 and control/5 with :not_running, :terminal and :lease_lost admission and no Approval or begin_attempt control; renewal and deadline wakes are the host's own.
